clue.text: Stages opening of Salome on revolving set

indicators.note: in an across clue the reversed piece sits on, that is just before, the letter from Salome
revolving turns the word for set round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to set is to gel, as a jelly does

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the start of Salome

explanation.surface: A production of Salome begins with its opening scene performed on a revolving stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stages' reads as a verb about putting on a play; it is the noun, the parts of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey or competition is divided into stages, each one called a leg.

clue.text: Learner keen for the most part to acquire good score on course

indicators.note: to acquire means the shortened word takes the learner's letter inside it
for the most part means all but the last letter of the word for keen is used

parts.note: keen means eager
L is the learner-driver abbreviation, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A keen novice golfer manages, mostly through enthusiasm, to post a fine score on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims EAGER to EAGE, and L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, completing a hole in two strokes under par is called an eagle, a very good score.

clue.text: Looking after number one is perhaps sole basis for the French Revolution

indicators.note: in a down clue the base sits underneath, so the fish comes below the reversed article
Revolution turns the French article round so it reads backwards

parts.note: les is the French plural form of the
sole is one example of a flatfish, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A historian claims self-interest was the sole real basis for the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French Revolution' looks like the historical event; it is the French article turned round. In a down clue the basis sits at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your own interests first, caring only for yourself, is the mark of a self-centred person.

clue.text: Singer is able to modulate after losing voice initially

parts.note: is able means can

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for modulate

parts.note: to modulate is to vary in pitch or tone

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist can still adjust their tone even after losing their voice at the start of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes V (voice's first letter) from VARY to leave ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a songbird, famous for its singing and kept as a pet for that reason.

clue.text: Marine creatures caught by the mouth

definitions.note: plural here, but the word for these reef animals is used for a mass of them too

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
oral means by the mouth, as medicine taken orally

explanation.surface: Sea animals being caught and eaten, swallowed straight down.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefs are built by tiny polyps, sea animals whose skeletons form the rocky mass.

clue.text: Cure backward child having tantrum after social worker's gone

indicators.note: backward means the word for child is read in reverse

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: gone says the insect's letters are removed from tantrum

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's social worker, an insect living in a colony

explanation.surface: A parent seeks a remedy for a difficult child whose tantrum started once the social worker left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns SON to NOS; 'gone' removes ANT from TANTRUM, leaving TRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or pet scheme for fixing things is called a nostrum, a supposed panacea.

clue.text: Once again make vital case for regime worried about dictator returning

indicators.note: the case for a word is its outer letters, the first and last of regime
about means the word for worried goes around the reversed name

parts.note: worried means ate, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: returning reads the dictator's name backwards

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Someone argues for reviving a regime that is anxious about a dictator coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin ruled Uganda in the 1970s; 'worried' means eaten away, as in what's eating you.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something back to life, restoring its energy, is to revive or reanimate it.

clue.text: Child's original feature?

definitions.note: read as child is, so the clue says the child is the rest

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Urtext
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A question about some distinctive feature a child was born with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's' is read as 'Child is', so the rest of the clue builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a mischievous, scruffy young child.

clue.text: Standing ovation ultimately lifts male social worker

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter lifts the insect, sitting on top of it

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is men only

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of ovation

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's social worker, an insect living in a colony

explanation.surface: A standing ovation at the end gives a boost to a male social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing ovation' looks like one phrase, but 'Standing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing water is still and not flowing, which is what stagnant water is.

clue.text: Bullet hit lazy person's drink

definitions.meaning: a bullet, especially a crude one
to hit hard with the fist
a sluggard is a lazy person; the 's reads as is
a gulp or swig of spirits

explanation.surface: A shot hits a layabout's glass of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: One short word covers a bullet, a punch, a sluggard and a swig of liquor.

clue.text: Official uniform worn by leaders of the opposition

indicators.note: worn by here says the uniform's word wraps round the leading letters

parts.note: uniform means regular, all alike

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of the and opposition

explanation.surface: An official dresses in uniform, as worn by the heads of the political opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters T and O go inside REGULAR, between its A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is an official who oversees an industry and enforces its rules.

clue.text: Mobile home owner's local area network is configured incorrectly

indicators.note: configured incorrectly says the letters are set up in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone in a caravan finds their home computer network has been set up badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile home' suggests a caravan; it is the shell an animal carries on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden mollusc carries its shell with it, so it owns a home that travels.

clue.text: Marking title ends in article being exchanged

indicators.note: the two ends of article are A and E, and one is swapped for the other in the word for title

parts.note: a heading is the title at the top of a page

explanation.surface: Someone marks up a document, swapping the ends of a heading in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'article' are A and E: swap the A of HEADING for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking someone's words means taking notice of them, paying attention to them.

clue.text: Lying hidden by Spooner's sport

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the sport's two syllables are swapped, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: curling is a sport played on ice with stones; said in two syllables, this is the first
the second syllable of the same ice sport

explanation.surface: Something lying hidden beside the Reverend Spooner's favourite game.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the sport as CUR-LING and swap the opening sounds: LUR-KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurking means waiting out of sight, concealed and ready to pounce.

clue.text: Start to perform hymn about divine spirit

indicators.note: about says the letters are turned around into a new order
start to takes the first letter of perform

explanation.surface: A choir begins to sing a hymn about a holy spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these minor goddesses were nature spirits of woods, rivers and seas.

clue.text: Role Mad Max almost played in theatrical production

indicators.note: played says the letters are acted out in a different arrangement
almost drops the final letter of Max

explanation.surface: An actor performs a role in a stage version of the Mad Max film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Max to MA before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage play with exaggerated characters and emotions.

clue.text: Seasonal manual working stopped by trade union

indicators.note: stopped by means the union's letters plug a gap in the rearranged word
working says the letters of manual are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Seasonal manual labour is halted by a union strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual working' reads as physical labour, but 'working' is the anagram signal on manual.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the season of fall: adjective form for the time between summer and winter.

clue.text: Sort of battery with energy storage unit

indicators.note: sort of says the letters of battery are sorted into another order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A type of battery used for storing energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A terabyte is a unit of data storage, a trillion bytes.

clue.text: College beginning to see dons hang around here

indicators.note: dons is read as puts on, the word for hang around wearing the letter inside it

parts.note: to loiter is to hang around idly

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of see

explanation.surface: A college where you can expect to see academics idling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like academics but means puts on: S goes inside LOITER. 'here' points back to the whole scene of dons pacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered arcade around a college quadrangle, just where dons would stroll.

clue.text: Insect found in decorator's drink

indicators.note: found in says the insect sits inside the decorator's word

parts.note: an icer decorates cakes with icing
a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: A fly turns up in a painter and decorator's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorator' suggests a painter; here it is someone icing cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice beer is a lager brewed by freezing so that some water is removed, making it stronger.

clue.text: Suspect clergyman is inexperienced

definitions.meaning: Reverend ... is the vicar among the suspects in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US)
a new, untrained person is described as raw or callow

explanation.surface: A dubious vicar turns out to be a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer still lacking practice is green, like unripe fruit; the Cluedo vicar shares the name.

clue.text: Well-mannered upper-class girl recruits new assistant for driver

indicators.note: recruits says the girl takes the other letters into her ranks

parts.note: gel is how a posh speaker says girl
a tee holds the golf ball for a driver shot

explanation.surface: A refined young lady takes on a fresh helper for her chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a chauffeur but is the golf club; a tee helps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and polite in manner, often with a hint of affectation.

clue.text: Anger caused by national pay having shilling deducted

indicators.note: deducted says the coin's letter is taken out of the word for pay

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: Workers are angered when a shilling is docked from the national pay rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate or annoy them, like a stinging plant.

clue.text: Evil British group losing money

indicators.note: losing means the money letter is dropped from the band's name

parts.note: Madness is a British ska-pop band of the 1980s

explanation.surface: A wicked British band ends up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' is the band Madness, losing M to give ADNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Badness is the noun for wickedness, as evil is.

clue.text: Marine creature is the "voice of the deep"

definitions.meaning: the sea fish also called the sea perch
the lowest male singing voice, deep in pitch

explanation.surface: A sea creature claims to speak for the ocean depths.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers a sea fish and the lowest singing voice, though pronounced differently.

clue.text: Guide that is on sale to the public

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
a new book or record is out when released for sale

explanation.surface: A guide that has been published for the public to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout goes ahead to find the way, and the Guides and Scouts are linked youth movements.

clue.text: Good suit clothing Englishman's frame

indicators.note: clothing says the word for suit wraps round the outer letters

parts.note: to suit is to befit

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outer letters, here the outside of Englishman

explanation.surface: A smart suit flatters an Englishman's build.
explanation.walkthrough: E and N, the frame of Englishman, go inside BEFIT after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun good, as in for the common good, means advantage or benefit.

clue.text: Defeat argument in favour of accepting reduced fortune

indicators.note: accepting says the trimmed word is taken inside

parts.note: an argument in favour is the case for

indicators.note: reduced cuts the last letter from the word for fortune

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A losing debater's case is weakened by a dwindling fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'argument in favour' is the case for something, so the word is the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down or beat them, as in a boxing match.

clue.text: Serpent recalled somewhat tongue-in-cheek answer

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The setter Serpent remembers giving a jokey reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serpent' is also the setter's own name, so the clue quietly signs itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a snake, especially in literary or biblical language.

clue.text: One lit hob somehow in the process of cooking

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone has lit a single hob and the dinner is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Food simmering at boiling point is being cooked; the phrase also means actively under way.

clue.text: Repeat the standard nonsense

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone is told to recite the usual drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: I'm surprised by rumour once wife's left

indicators.note: read as wife is left: W, the abbreviation for wife, turns into L, the abbreviation for left

parts.note: word once meant news or rumour, an old sense

explanation.surface: Someone reacts in shock to gossip that the wife has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'wife's left' as 'wife is left': W becomes L in WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of astonishment, as in good heavens, uses the title of God.
